key_insight: Denoising pairwise distances before spectral embedding can reveal nonlinear geometry and separate clusters with coincident centers, even under strong noise.
engineering_relevance: The approach could improve embedding and clustering pipelines for high-dimensional measurements whose raw distances are distorted by accumulated noise.
method: Estimate latent signal distances using cross-fitted projections.
Select a neighborhood radius from the sample and build a random geometric graph.
Compute spectral embeddings and recursively extract clusters.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports manifold-model guarantees and numerical studies showing improved geometry recovery and clustering, but provides no dataset details or quantitative results.
watch_item: Strong-noise guarantees depend on modeling assumptions, with additional conditions required when total noise energy exceeds total signal energy.
paper_title: Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs
